subject: Usage and surge-hedge proposal for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Li <andrew@skyline.ai>, Melissa Jiang <melissa.jiang@skyline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Usage and surge-hedge proposal for upcoming renewal

Andrew / Melissa —

Thanks again for the call today. I pulled together a short, pragmatic proposal to cover the usage volatility you described (spikes from seasonal campaigns) without committing you to a large upfront uplift. The attached skyline_q3_usage.csv shows the hourly token spikes across your production endpoints for the last 90 days; key observations:

- Baseline monthly tokens: ~1.1B (steady-state).
- Top-10 spike days average 3.8x baseline for 6–12 hour windows.
- Model mix shifting to larger context runs (avg tokens per request +40% q/q).

Proposal (high level):
1) Add a 25% committed uplift (to 1.375B) with an auto-burst pool for up to 50% of baseline for temporary surges.
2) Keep current per-token pricing for baseline tier; apply a 10% surcharge on burst tokens (only when auto-burst is consumed).
3) Provide a one-time credit to offset migration/config work: $15k applied on first invoice.

Expected ROI/impact: with the above hedge you avoid throttling during spikes and reduce emergency overages. Attached roi_snapshot_skyline_q3.pdf models three scenarios and shows net savings vs pay-as-you-go in aggressive spike months.

Next steps I recommend:
- Confirm you can accept a 25% commit uplift as an initial hedge.
- If accepted, I’ll draft the amendment and loop Legal/Procurement for a quick 7–10 day turnaround.

If it helps, Marissa and Grace are copied to weigh in on pricing levers and any SLA language we should include.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0183

Attachments: skyline_q3_usage.csv, roi_snapshot_skyline_q3.pdf, proposed_commit_table.xlsx
From: Andrew Li <andrew@skyline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Melissa Jiang <melissa.jiang@skyline.ai>, procurement@skyline.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage and surge-hedge proposal for upcoming renewal

Ben — appreciate the quick follow. I reviewed the CSV and the ROI doc. A few clarifying questions before we commit:

1) For the auto-burst pool, is there any preemption/queueing if the region is under extreme load (we run in us-west primarily)?
2) Can the 25% uplift be staged over two quarters (12.5% now, 12.5% next quarter) to smooth our budget?
3) The 10% surcharge on burst tokens — can that be converted into a fixed burst uplift fee (we prefer predictable line items on the invoice).

Also, two asks from Procurement (copied):
- They want a short addendum with clear termination/true-up mechanics.
- They will need SOC2 evidence and the token retention policy referenced in the amendment.

If we can get those answered, procurement is willing to fast-track.

Thanks —
Andrew
Head of Product — Skyline AI
andrew@skyline.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Li <andrew@skyline.ai>, Melissa Jiang <melissa.jiang@skyline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, procurement@skyline.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage and surge-hedge proposal for upcoming renewal

Thanks Andrew — quick answers inline so procurement can move: 

1) Auto-burst behavior: the burst pool is region-local and prioritized behind Reserved capacity. In an extreme region-wide outage we fall back to nearest compatible region (we’ll include explicit fallback language). We’ll also enable graceful degradation (rate-limited responses with a 503+Retry-After for non-critical endpoints) if you want that behavior documented.

2) Staged uplift: yes — we can structure the commit as a two-step uplift (12.5% on signing, rest after 90 days). We’ll reflect that in the amendment payment schedule.

3) Convert surcharge: we can offer a fixed monthly burst allowance fee instead of a percentage surcharge — recommendation: fixed fee that covers up to 40% of baseline burst minutes, then per-token pricing after that. I’ll put the exact numbers in the contract appendix.

On SOC2 and token retention: attaching a standard evidence packet and the retention policy excerpt (I’ve added links to the Drive in the related_links field). Marissa to confirm SLA/termination language.

If that all looks good to you Procurement team, we can move to a redline-ready doc this week.

Best,
Ben

Attachments: proposed_commit_table.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Andrew Li <andrew@skyline.ai>, Melissa Jiang <melissa.jiang@skyline.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, procurement@skyline.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage and surge-hedge proposal for upcoming renewal

Andrew / Melissa —

I reviewed Ben's adjustments and the proposed commercial structure. From a pricing and risk perspective the staged uplift + fixed burst fee is reasonable and aligns with how we’ve rolled similar customers. A couple of small asks for the amendment: 

- Add a 30-day true-up window following any month where burst consumption exceeds allowance by >25%.
- Preserve the ability for Skyline to reduce committed baseline (with 60-day notice) once per contract year with a 5% re-price floor.

If Procurement is OK with those two bullets I’ll approve the terms and ask Legal to produce a redline. Ben — send me the updated appendix and I’ll queue Legal.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147
